chunks.arabic_text: رِجَالُ الْكَشِّيِّ: مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ مَسْعُودٍ، عَنِ عَبْدِ اللَّهِ بْنِ مُحَمَّدٍ، عَن أَبِيهِ، عَنِ إِسْمَاعِيلَ بْنِ عَبْدِ الْخَالِقِ قَالَ

translations.en: Rijal al-Kashshi: Muhammad ibn Masud, from Abdullah ibn Muhammad, from his father, from Ismail ibn Abd al-Khaliq, who said:

chunks.arabic_text: ذَكَرَ أَبُو عَبْدِ اللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ السَّلَامُ أَبِيهِ فَقَالَ: صَلَّى اللَّهُ عَلَى أَبِيكَ ثَلَاثًا

translations.en: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) remembered my father and said: May Allah bless your father – thrice.

en.summary: This narration from Rijal al-Kashshi highlights the personal intimacy of Imam al-Sadiq (AS) with the family of Ismail ibn Abd al-Khaliq, a notable companion, by invoking divine blessings (salawat) upon his father three times. This specific tripling of blessings underscores the high status of the father within the Shia scholarly network and reflects the Imam's role in validating the spiritual standing of his companions' lineages. It serves as a testament to the deep, familial bonds that characterized the relationship between the Imams and the early transmitters of Hadith.
en.seo_question: What did Imam al-Sadiq say about the father of Ismail ibn Abd al-Khaliq?

key_terms.أَبُو عَبْدِ اللَّهِ: Abu Abdillah, a title for Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq
